whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives

become: It can take years of practice to become a skilled musician.
engineer: to design, build, or skilfully arrange something, especially something difficult
They had to engineer a clever fix using only spare parts.
however: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something previously said
The plan sounded good; however, it proved too expensive.
training: the process of teaching or practising a skill
Anyone who has stopped training for a year and then started again will recognise the pattern.
available: able to be obtained, used or reached
Tickets for the concert are still available online.
goes: moves or travels from one place to another
He goes to the gym every morning before work.
beyond: further away than, or outside the limits of, something
The hiking trail continues far beyond the edge of the forest.
tasks: pieces of work that must be done
She listed all the tasks she needed to finish before Friday.
production: the process of making or growing something in large quantities
Production at the factory slowed after the machinery broke down.
line: a long thin mark or stroke
She drew a straight line across the page with a ruler.
there: in, at, or to that place; used to show that something exists
There is a small cafe just around the corner.
longer-term: relating to a more extended future period
The committee is now focused on longer-term solutions to the crisis.
hope: a feeling of expectation or desire for something to happen
She never lost hope that things would improve.
too: The height of the band carries information too.
start: the beginning or first part of something
The meeting got off to a slow start.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
move: Engineers designed the bridge deck to move slightly in strong wind.
gradually: slowly, over a period of time
The town gradually grew into a busy commercial centre.
up: towards a higher place or position
Neighbourhoods with few trees and little open space heat up fastest.
later: at a time after the one mentioned
They met again later that year at a conference.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
even: used to emphasise something surprising or extreme
Your body keeps track of time even in a dark room.
also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
becoming: The town is becoming a popular spot for young families.
important: It is important to drink enough water during exercise.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
find: I finally found my keys under the sofa.
ways: It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes the weather.
stack: to arrange things in a neat pile, one on top of another
She stacked the plates carefully in the cupboard.
together: with each other; combined into one group or place
Sourdough relies on wild yeasts and bacteria living together in a starter.
improve: make or become better than before
Regular practice will improve your writing skills over time.
performance: how well a person, machine, or system functions or carries out a task
Engineers tested the engine's performance under extremely cold weather conditions.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
global: relating to the whole world; worldwide
Climate change is a global problem requiring international cooperation.
system: a set of things working together as a connected whole
The school introduced a new system for tracking student attendance.
serious: requiring careful thought or attention; not casual
He gave a serious answer instead of joking as usual.
concentration: the ability to focus, or the gathering of something in one place
Reading late at night can weaken concentration the next morning.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
region: an area of a country or the world with particular features
The mountainous region attracts hikers from all over the world.
earthquake: a sudden violent shaking of the ground
The earthquake caused significant damage to older buildings in the city.
fire: the flame, light and heat produced by burning
They gathered around the fire to keep warm at night.
political: relating to government, public affairs, or politics
The debate quickly turned into a political argument about taxes.
crisis: a time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger
The company faced a financial crisis after losing its biggest client.
disrupt: to interrupt or interfere with the normal course of something
Heavy snowfall could disrupt flights across the entire region.
worldwide: The number of garments produced worldwide has roughly doubled since 2000.
during: throughout the course of a period of time
She stayed awake during the entire overnight bus journey.
pandemic: a disease outbreak occurring across a wide area or worldwide
The pandemic forced many businesses to close their doors temporarily.
shortage: a state in which there is not enough of something needed
The drought led to a severe water shortage.
forced: made to do something against one's will
Heavy rain forced the organizers to cancel the outdoor concert.
car: a road vehicle with four wheels used for carrying passengers
They drove a small car through the narrow mountain roads.
pause: a short stop in an action, speech, or process
There was an awkward pause before anyone answered the question.
though: She smiled, though she was clearly exhausted from the trip.
needed: The volunteers brought all the supplies needed for the rescue.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'
The missing words had to be invented, and many were.
cheap: Street food here is cheap and surprisingly delicious.
simple: easy to understand or do; not complicated
He gave a simple explanation that even a child could understand.
tool: a device or implement used to carry out a particular task
Towns have opened tool libraries with ladders, sanders and tile cutters.
policy: a plan of action agreed by a government, business, or group
The company changed its policy on remote work last month.
because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
power: electricity or energy supplied to run a device
The whole neighborhood lost power during the storm.
centres: plural of centre; main locations of an activity or organization
Community centres offer free classes for job seekers every week.
weapons: objects used to cause damage or harm in a fight
The most advanced chips power everything from data centres to weapons.
limit: the greatest amount or extent allowed
There is a strict limit on how much luggage you can bring.
buy: to obtain something by paying money for it
They plan to buy a small house near the coast next year.
make: to produce, create or cause something
Good lighting can make a small room feel much larger.
caught: captured, seized, or stopped partway through an action
bị bắt, bị chặn giữa chừng
The thief was caught trying to climb over the fence.
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
rival: a person or thing competing with another for the same goal
đối thủ, đối thủ cạnh tranh
The two coffee shops became bitter rivals within a year.
powers: strong and influential countries or organizations
Global powers met to discuss the new trade agreement.
asked: put a question to someone or requested something
He asked the librarian where he could find books on astronomy.
choose: to select one thing from a number of possibilities
Students can choose between three different elective subjects.
sides: groups or positions opposing each other in a dispute or conflict
The negotiators tried to find a solution that satisfied both sides.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
followed: came after something in time or order
A period of calm followed the storm.
skill: the ability to do something well, gained through training or practice
Cooking well takes years of practice and skill to master.
politics: activities and debates concerned with governing a country or area
She avoided discussing politics at the family dinner table.
middle: the point or part that is equally distant from the edges or ends
She placed the vase right in the middle of the table.
tension: a feeling of unease, strain, or unresolved conflict
There was noticeable tension in the room before the results were announced.
bring: to carry or take something to a place, or to start a legal case
Lawyers plan to bring a case against the company next month.
new: not existing before; recently made, discovered or experienced
They moved into a new apartment near the city centre.
investment: money, time, or effort put into something to gain future benefit
Buying the small shop turned out to be a wise investment.
look: to direct one's eyes in order to see
Look both ways carefully before crossing the busy street.
safer: less likely to cause harm or danger
The new crossing is much safer for schoolchildren.
locations: The chain plans to open ten new locations next year.
brings: carries or takes something to a place
Spring always brings warmer weather and blooming flowers to the region.
pressure: a feeling of stress caused by demands or difficulties
The manager felt under pressure to finish the project by Friday.
responded: The government responded to the criticism with a new policy.
offering: presenting something for someone to accept or refuse
The airline is offering free meals on long-haul flights this month.
subsidies: sums of money given by a government to support an industry
Farmers rely heavily on subsidies during years of low prices.
home: the place where a person lives
After the long trip, it felt good to finally be home.
hoping: wishing or expecting something to happen
We are hoping for good weather during the festival.
supply: to provide something that is needed
The factory supplies parts to car makers across the region.
secure: The bridge was made secure before traffic was allowed back on.
critics: people who express disapproval or judge the faults of something
nhà phê bình, người chỉ trích
Critics praised the novel's honest portrayal of grief.
warn: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem
Some researchers warn against talking about a loneliness epidemic.
raise: to increase the amount, level, or position of something
The landlord decided to raise the rent again this year.
costs: requires the payment of a specified amount of money
A round trip by taxi costs more than the entire bus fare for a week.
waste: material that is no longer needed, or a careless use of resources
The change in thinking has been to stop treating rain as waste.
public: provided by the state for everyone; open to all people
The new library is open to the public every day of the week.
if: introducing a condition on which something depends
If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
chase: to pursue something in order to catch or achieve it
Several countries are racing to chase the same technological breakthrough.
goal: an aim or desired result that someone works towards
Her main goal this year is to save enough money to travel.
spreading: extending over a larger area or reaching more people or places
She was spreading butter evenly across each slice of bread.
widely: over a large area, or by many people
Cheap substitutes existed throughout history, and they were widely used.
reduces: makes something smaller or less in amount
Regular exercise reduces the risk of many chronic illnesses.
risk: the possibility of something bad or dangerous happening
Investing in a new business always carries some risk.
gives: The charity gives food and shelter to homeless families.
efficiency: the ability to work well without wasting time or resources
The new engine improved fuel efficiency by ten percent.
challenge: something that tests one's abilities in a difficult way
Learning a new language later in life is a real challenge.
join: to become a member of a group or take part in something
Many students join the debate club in their first year.
simply: in an easy or straightforward way; just, merely
She simply smiled and walked away without saying a word.
another: one more, or a different one, of the same kind
Could I have another cup of coffee, please?
replaceable: able to be replaced by something else
Most parts of the old machine are cheap and replaceable.
link: Researchers found a link between poor sleep and low mood.
building: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or office
The old building was renovated into modern apartments last year.
people: human beings in general, considered as a group of individuals
Many people prefer walking to work during the warm summer months.
technicians: people skilled in the practical use of machines or equipment
Technicians checked every cable before the concert began.
designers: people who plan how things will look or work
Several designers competed to create the city's new logo.
kind: a type or category of something
This kind of bread takes several hours to rise properly.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
pays: gives money in exchange for goods or a service
He always pays for dinner whenever they eat out together.
graduates: people who have completed a degree or course of study
Many graduates struggle to find jobs in their field right away.
good: of high quality, favourable, or beneficial
It was a good decision to leave early before the storm.
rather: She chose to walk rather than take the crowded bus.
leaving: going away from a place, or allowing something to remain
Leaving the party early, she missed the surprise announcement.
better-paid: receiving a higher salary or wage than others
Many young graduates leave home in search of better-paid jobs abroad.
abroad: in or to a foreign country
He spent a year studying abroad before returning home to graduate.
reminder: something that makes you remember something
The scar on his arm was a reminder of the accident.
technology: the practical application of scientific knowledge, especially in industry
Advances in technology have made remote work much easier.
belongs: is the property of, or a proper part of, something
This particular skill belongs to a select group of expert craftsmen.
nation: a large body of people united by common government, history or culture
The whole nation celebrated when the treaty was finally signed.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
lies: is positioned somewhere, or says untrue things (he/she/it)
The answer to the puzzle lies in the very first clue.
cooperation: the act of working together with others towards a shared aim
The project succeeded thanks to close cooperation between the two teams.
